subject: Session archive vs flush — default behavior and erasure steps
body:
From: Alice Wong <alice.wong@fintegrra.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@fintegrra.com
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify — what gets archived vs flushed by default when our users end sessions

Hi Jonas,

Quick follow-up from our security review:
We need a concise statement of Redwood's default behavior for interactive sessions (web chat + SDK streaming) — specifically:
- Which elements are archived (stored persistently) vs flushed (ephemeral) immediately on session end? Examples we care about: full request text, model-generated tokens (streamed partials), final model response, KV cache snapshots, debug/traces, and embeddings generated as part of the session.
- What is the default retention window for each category (days)?
- What steps do we follow to prove erasure for a given user/session if Fintegrra requests deletion (and how long after a delete action before backups/logs no longer contain the data)?

We're trying to map this into our internal control doc and need this by EOD PT.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Wong
Head of Security
Fintegrra Inc.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify — what gets archived vs flushed by default when our users end sessions

Thanks for the clear list, Alice. Looping in Kimberly for policy specifics and Marissa for erasure runbook / evidence. Below are the things I'll call out — Kimberly, please confirm and add exact TL;DR windows we can share.

High level (draft):
- Requests (raw user input) — archived by default for hosted accounts in us region for 90 days; EU-hosted can be configured to shorter windows or auto-delete on a customer-managed TTL.
- Streamed partial tokens (intermediate fragments sent while model generates) — not persisted beyond the streaming buffer by default; only finalized tokens are considered for storage unless customer enables session transcript capture.
- Final model response (finalized output) — persisted by default and included in the 90-day window; can be excluded via customer settings or enterprise contracts.
- KV cache snapshots (inference runtime caches) — ephemeral; flushed at session termination and not stored as user-visible artifacts.
- Embeddings generated during the session — treated as derivative artifacts and stored only if customer activates the embedding export feature; otherwise not persisted beyond job lifecycle.

Kimberly / Marissa: anything immediate you'd change?

Cheers,
Jonas
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Alice Wong <alice.wong@fintegrra.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify — what gets archived vs flushed by default when our users end sessions

Hi Alice, Jonas — thanks for the draft. I added concrete items below with the canonical wording we use in customer-facing docs. Attaching a compact retention matrix (redwood_retention_matrix_v1.csv) that maps artifacts to default windows and erasure paths.

Canonical answers (default hosted behavior unless otherwise contracted):
1) Raw requests / user inputs
- Default: Persisted for 90 days in hosted (us) by default. Purpose: telemetry, model improvement opt-out (customers can disable), fraud/abuse detection.
- Erasure: Customer sends an erasure request (API or support). We queue the request -> mark artifacts for deletion -> purge primary store within 48 hours. Backups: standard backup retention may include records up to 30 additional days; backups are overwritten on normal schedule and will not be restored for single-object requests. We provide deletion evidence (index checksums + timestamps) within 5 business days.

2) Streamed partial tokens (transient fragments)
- Default: Not written to durable storage by default; stored only in in-memory streaming buffers and ephemeral logs used for debugging that are rotated every 24 hours and retained for a maximum of 7 days if debug logging is enabled.
- Erasure: For accounts with debug logs enabled, deletion removes durable rotated logs within 48 hours of a request; ephemeral buffers vanish at session end.

3) Final model responses (finalized outputs)
- Default: Persisted 90 days by default. This includes outputs generated synchronously or at stream completion.
- Optional: Customers can opt-out of storing outputs or set custom TTL via account settings or enterprise contract.

4) KV cache and runtime caches
- Default: Ephemeral; never persisted as part of user records. Cache snapshots are not part of exported evidence. They are flushed on session termination and garbage-collected immediately.

5) Embeddings and derived vectors
- Default: Not stored unless the customer explicitly enables embedding export or uses a Redwood-managed embeddings route. If enabled: persistent and subject to customer-configured retention; default 365 days for embedding indices when enabled.

6) Debug/traces/diagnostic spans
- Default: Diagnostic traces are sampled and retained for 30 days for hosted accounts; they are scrubbed of PII by default and tied to request ids. Customers can request a narrower window.

7) Audit and billing records
- Default: Billing line items and usage aggregates persist per finance policy (7 years for invoices); individual request-level billing traces are retained for 1 year.

Proof of erasure (how we demonstrate deletion)
- Primary deletion: object-level deletion with audit entry (timestamp, request id, operator).
- Backup window: We disclose that backups may include the object for a short window (up to 30 days), and we provide a remediation timetable and attestations for when the backups will no longer contain the data.
- Evidence package: redwood provides a deletion report (JSON manifest + checksums), a dated index search demonstrating absence, and (if required) a signed attestation for compliance teams. We can deliver within 5 business days for off-cycle requests or faster under an SLA.

Region note
- EU-hosted customers: default defaults are shorter and residency-bound; we can configure auto-purge at 7/30/90 day windows per contract. For customers requiring strict minimal retention (e.g., GDPR data minimization), we recommend Private deployments or dedicated retention profiles.

Attachments in this thread:
- redwood_retention_matrix_v1.csv (mapping artifact -> default window -> erasure path)
- soc2-evidence-stub.pdf (high level description of what evidence looks like)

If you want, Marissa can provide the specific API call sequence for a programmatic erasure and the typical webhook/confirmation flow.

Kimberly Park
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify — what gets archived vs flushed by default when our users end sessions

Hi Alice — brief follow up with the erasure runbook steps we use internally (can be shared as a one-pager):
1) Intake: Confirm requester identity and scope (user id / session id / timeframe).
2) Mark: Mark all matching artifacts in the search index as "to-delete" and record a deletion ticket (internal ID).
3) Primary purge: Remove objects from primary stores (S3/NoSQL) — completes within 48 hours.
4) Index rebuild: Rebuild affected index shards to remove references (complete within 72 hours).
5) Backup handling: Log the request to the backup retention team; backups are rotated and will naturally expire; we can schedule an expedited scrub for high-priority legal requests (timelines provided in the evidence package).
6) Evidence: Provide the deletion manifest and index absence screenshots; escalate to security for signed attestation if required.

API example: POST /v1/admin/erase {"scope":"user:alice@fintegrra.com","from":"2028-01-01","to":"2028-03-19"} -> returns job id -> webhook on status change.

If Fintegrra needs an SLA that shortens the backup window or mandates immediate wipe from backups, we can propose a Dedicated/Private option in the contract.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference
